# Candidate absorber materials
- Absorber-F2: dense alloy with a short radiation length.
- Absorber-F1: dense alloy, different composition.
- Absorber-F3: standard structural absorber.
All three can be machined to the required plate tolerances.

# Activation study, 2026
Absorber samples were irradiated at the test facility and the results were scaled to 10 years of nominal running (FLUKA cross-check).
Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown:
- Absorber-F2: 85 uSv/h  (long-lived activation products dominate)
- Absorber-F1: 12 uSv/h
- Absorber-F3: 6 uSv/h
Radiation-protection limit for hands-on maintenance access: 20 uSv/h.

# Meeting notes 2026-05-14
The mechanical support design was reviewed and is compatible with every candidate absorber.

Water cooling at 18 C. The heat load is dominated by the front-end electronics.

The silicon-pad readout and front-end ASIC are common to all absorber options.

# Schedule
Absorber choice in Q3; prototype beam test next year.

input.justification:
Absorber-F1 with 2 mm plates is recommended based on the following analysis:

MATERIAL SELECTION:
Absorber-F2 is eliminated due to excessive activation (85 uSv/h after one week cooldown, exceeding the 20 uSv/h limit for hands-on maintenance). This leaves Absorber-F1 and Absorber-F3 as viable candidates.

Between F1 and F3, Absorber-F1 is selected because:
1. It is described as a "dense alloy," which typically provides superior energy resolution in electromagnetic calorimeters due to shorter radiation length and more compact shower development.
2. F1 meets the activation constraint with 12 uSv/h, well below the 20 uSv/h limit.
3. As a denser material, F1 should provide better energy resolution compared to F3 ("standard structural absorber").

PLATE THICKNESS SELECTION:
2 mm plate thickness is selected (the minimum allowed) because:
1. In sampling calorimeters, thinner absorber plates provide better sampling frequency, leading to improved energy resolution.
2. The stochastic term in energy resolution (dominant at 100 GeV) improves with better sampling.
3. All candidates can be machined to required tolerances at this thickness.

This configuration is expected to achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV while meeting all hard constraints (activation limit and mechanical manufacturability).

Dense materials with thin plates typically achieve resolutions well below 4.5% at 100 GeV in electromagnetic calorimeters.
